He arrives a day after President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed a new Ukrainian offensive in the Kursk region of Russia and said that North Korean troops were fighting next to the Russian forces there.
“In the areas of Kursk’s operation, new assaults have been produced,” Zelensky said during his Friday’s direction, added: “Russia has once again deployed North Korean soldiers along with their troops.”
According to Mr. Zelensky, a “significant number” of enemy troops was destroyed. He did not give details, but said the losses were in hundreds.
The Russian Ministry of Defense said on Saturday that it had repelled a Ukrainian counterattack in the Kursk region.
Russia said Friday that their forces had captured the Mining City of Toretsk in its last advance in the East Region of Donetsk, where Ukrainian defenses are crunching. Ukrainian officials did not confirm the report.
South Korea’s army said last month that he suspected that North Korea was preparing to send additional troops to Russia after their soldiers suffered strong casualties.
North Korea has been supplying a large amount of artillery and other conventional weapons to Russia, and last October also sent around 10,000-12,000 troops, according to US intelligence, Surcoreana and Ukraine.
